scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to delete their stepbrother's profile on their Nintendo Switch. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, the person had to watch their stepbrother for a week while their dad and his mom were on a trip. They brought their Switch along because they wanted something to do during their long train commute to school. The stepbrother wanted to play on it, and it actually helped distract him while the person studied. So, they created a new profile for the stepbrother to keep their saves separate. When they got back to school, they got annoyed because they had to click on their profile every time they started a game or went to the eShop. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. Now, during Thanksgiving, the stepbrother found out his Zelda save was gone and got upset, even crying a little. The dad thinks it was mean. Hmm, so the main issue here is deleting someone else's profile without their knowledge or consent. The person felt annoyed by having to switch profiles, but the stepbrother was using it as a way to enjoy his time and maybe even as a distraction during a stressful period. I think about ownership here. The Switch is the person's property, so they have the right to manage profiles on it. But the stepbrother was using it with permission, and the person created the profile for him. So, there's a bit of a balance between ownership and shared use. Deleting the profile without telling the stepbrother seems like it could be hurtful, especially if the stepbrother was emotionally invested in his games, like Zelda. The fact that he cried shows how upset he was. The dad's reaction also indicates that it was seen as mean. On the other hand, the person didn't want to deal with the inconvenience of switching profiles. Maybe they could have communicated their feelings instead of deleting the profile. They could have talked to the stepbrother about it or found another way to manage the profiles without deleting them. So, considering all this, I think it was wrong because it involved deleting something the stepbrother was using and enjoying without his consent, which caused him emotional distress. It would have been better to communicate and find a solution together rather than taking unilateral action.
